Q1. Line DE is prolonged to point F by double centering. Length F'F" is 0.84 ft. Length DE and EF is 721.44 ft and 614.23 ft, respectively. The angular error introduced in a single plunging is
IIfieldProgram T — partial

  • A) 0°4'42"
  • B) 0°1'5"
  • C) 0°2'21"
  • D) 0°2'10"
\(F'F" = 0.84 \text{ ft}\) \(\dfrac{0.84}{2} = 0.42 \text{ ft}\) \(\tan\theta = \dfrac{0.42}{614.23}\) \(\theta = 0°2'21"\)

Answer: C

Instructor Kirk TAug 07
F' and F" are additional measurements on point F and therefore we are looking for the average error which is why we divide by 2. If we had a F"' then we would divide by 3 to give us the average.
Q2. Determine the volume between sta 4+73 and sta 3+89 rounded to the nearest hundred CY.
IIIarea

  • A) 8400 CY
  • B) 2100 CY
  • C) 8200 CY
  • D) 33000 CY
Plan scale to real world ground scale: \(1\ \text{in}^{2} = 40' \times 10' = 400\ \text{ft}^{2}\) \(\text{Sta}\ 4{+}73\ \text{Area} = 5.43\ \text{in}^{2} \times \dfrac{400\ \text{ft}^{2}}{\text{in}^{2}} = 2172\ \text{ft}^{2}\) \(\text{Sta}\ 3{+}89\ \text{Area} = 7.82\ \text{in}^{2} \times \dfrac{400\ \text{ft}^{2}}{\text{in}^{2}} = 3128\ \text{ft}^{2}\) Using average end area method to calculate volume: \(V = \left(\dfrac{A_1 + A_2}{2}\right) \times L\) \(V = \dfrac{2172\ \text{ft}^{2} + 3128\ \text{ft}^{2}}{2} \times (473 - 389) = 222600\ \text{ft}^{3}\) \(V = 222600\ \text{ft}^{3} \times \dfrac{1\ \text{yd}^{3}}{27\ \text{ft}^{3}} = 8244.44\ \text{CY} \approx 8200\ \text{CY}\)

Answer: C
Q3. Which of the following are true statements:
1. (A) Random error can be present in all surveying measurements.
2. (B) Random error can be either positive or negative.
3. (C) Random errors are typically caused by factors beyond the surveyor's control.
4. (D) Random errors can still remain after all mistakes and systemic errors have been eliminated.
Itheory
  • A) C, D
  • B) A, D
  • C) B, C
  • D) A, B, C, D
All of the options are true of random errors. As the name implies, random errors occur in all calculations, can be positive or negative, and outside the control of a surveyor.
Answer: D
Q4. An area of a parcel shown on a map is 8728 ft². If the map scale factor is 0.99756, the actual ground area is
IIIarea
  • A) 8749.35 ft²
  • B) 8706.70 ft²
  • C) 8685.46 ft²
  • D) 8770.75 ft²
If the map scale factor is really 0.99756, that means that our current area is too small. So we must divided by the square of the factor (since a map scale factor is only for one dimension).
\(\dfrac{8728}{(0.99756)^{2}} = 8770.75 ft^{2}\)

Answer: D
Student/instructor discussion:

Instructor Kirk TJun 27
No would remain the same by dividing by the greater than 1 value. A greater than 1 value means the scale factor should reduce the actual ground area.
Q5. In a leveling field book, the correct procedure for checking the computed elevations is to
IIlevel
  • A) repeat all computations twice
  • B) average all backsights and foresight
  • C) subtract the sum of the foresights from the sum of the backsights and check to see if this number added to the start elevation equals the end elevation
  • D) add and subtract backsight and foresight starting from the last course to the first course
Subtract the sum of the foresights from the sum of the backsights and check to see if this number added to the start elevation equals the end elevation is the correct procedure to ensure accuracy.
Answer: C
Q6. What is the purpose of plunging a surveying instrument?
IIfield
  • A) To increase the accuracy of a recorded measurement by averaging in another measurement on the same point while the instrument is in the inverted position.
  • B) To lower the instrument to the lowest possible height in order to take the BS and FS readings without adjusting the location.
  • C) To take the next measurement on the next point without a new setup point.
  • D) To increase the accuracy of a recorded measurement by providing another measurement to compare which is closest to the known point.
The purpose of plunging an instrument is to take a second measurement on the same point. The second reading is then averaged with the first measurement in order to increase the accuracy of the recorded measurement on the point. The would balance out and negate errors due to nearly all the maladjustments of the instrument.
Answer: A

V.N.Dec 10

Instructor Kirk TDec 13
That is correct. Plunging means that you rotate the instrument along both the vertical and horizontal axis 180 degrees. By doing so, you increase the accuracy of the shot taken.
Q7. The area of the figure is
IIIarea

  • A) 20250 yd²
  • B) 2222 yd²
  • C) 20000 yd²
  • D) 2250 yd²

Area of triangles: \(\dfrac{(100\times 20) + (50\times 20) + (150\times 50)}{2} = 5250\) Area of rectangle: \(300 \times 50 = 15000\) Total Area: \(\text{Total Area} = 5250 + 15000 = 20250\ \text{ft}^{2}\) \(\dfrac{20250}{9} = 2250\ \text{yd}^{2}\)

Answer: D
Q8. The central angle of the horizontal curve is
Vhc

  • A) 89°24'8"
  • B) 86°48'32"
  • C) 87°6'28"
  • D) 83°37'4"

Tangent of the curve creates a 90 degree angle with the radius. Calculate the angle between the vertical line through the BVC and the radius (angle DCB): \(\text{angle DCB} = 180° - 44°42'4" - 90° = 45°17'56"\) Opposite angles of a line intersecting two parallel lines are equal: \(\text{angle DCB} = \text{angle ABC}\) Add angle ABC and angle ABE: \(\Delta = 45°17'56" + 41°48'32"\) \(\Delta = 87°6'28"\)

Q9. A transit is setup over Point A with an instrument height of 4.72 feet. The elevation of Point A is 347.72 ft. The zenith angle to a target with a rod reading of 5.21 feet on Point B is 102°43'52". The slope distance between the transit and the target is 321.73 ft. The vertical difference between Point A and Point B is
IIstadia
  • A) −72.2
  • B) 70.9
  • C) −70.9
  • D) −71.39

\(4.72 - 5.21 - (321.73)\sin(102°43'52" - 90°) = -71.39\ \text{ft}\)

Answer: D
Q10. Line CD is offset 11 ft to the north. Central angle = 90°. The curve distance AB is:
VhcProgram S — partial

  • A) 24.41 ft
  • B) 17.28 ft
  • C) 27.88 ft
  • D) 21.99 ft

The tangent offset here would be the distance from that horizontal line B and an imaginary horizontal line on A. A tangent offset starts from the tangent of a curve and ends at an offset to that line (parallel line). We see here that the tangent (T) at the point at the bottom of the curve (PT) can only move parallel in the x-direction so we know that the problem is referring to the tangent from point A. From here if we subtract the radius (point A vertically down until line CD) and 11', we get 14' offset. This is our tangent offset. \(\text{tangent offset} = 25 - 11 = 14\ \text{ft}\) \(14 = R(1 - \cos I) = 25(1 - \cos I)\) \(I = 63°53'46"\) \(\text{arc AB} = 2\pi R \times \dfrac{63°53'46"}{360°}\) \(\text{arc AB} = 2\pi(25) \times \dfrac{63°53'46"}{360°}\) \(\text{arc AB} = 27.88\ \text{ft}\)

Answer: C

Q12. On a standard topographic map with a scale 1:50,000, a ground distance of 21,625 ft would be represented by a map distance of
IVphoto

  • B) 7.12 inches
  • C) 0.43 inches

If the problem doesn't state what 1:50000 means then you can assume it is 1 in : 50000 in. \(\dfrac{1}{50000} = \dfrac{x}{21625(12\ \text{in}/\text{ft})}\) \(x = 5.19\ \text{inches}\)

Q13. If the area shaded is the amount of excavation at each cross section, what is the total volume to be removed along this stretch of roadway?
IIIarea

  • A) 33498 cu yds
  • B) 25851 cu yds
  • C) 29685 cu yds
  • D) 31679 cu yds
Recall that the area of a triangle is (base x height)/2. This could be any base times its corresponding perpendicular height. Let's start with Sta 236+78: \(\text{height of triangle} = \dfrac{230}{3.5} = 65.71'\) \(\text{area} = \dfrac{\text{base} \times \text{height}}{2} = \dfrac{140 \times 65.71}{2} = 4599.7\ \text{ft}^{2}\) Area of Sta 238+96: \(\text{area} = \dfrac{\text{base} \times \text{height}}{2} = \dfrac{50 \times 72.15}{2} = 1803.75\ \text{ft}^{2}\) Total volume of excavation: \(V = L\left(\dfrac{A_1 + A_2}{2}\right) = (23896 - 23678)\left(\dfrac{4599.7 + 1803.75}{2}\right)\) \(V = 697976\ \text{ft}^{3} = 25851\ \text{yd}^{3}\)

Answer: B

Q15. Which of the following instruments would be most useful for underground mapping?
IIfield
  • A) Total Station
  • B) Bathometer
  • C) Altimeter
  • D) Gyrotheodolite
A gyrotheodolite is composed of a gyroscope mounted to a theodolite. It is used to determine the orientation of true north without visibly seeing astrological stars. It is used in mine surveying and tunnel engineering. An altimeter is an instrument that measures the altitude of an object above a fixed point. It is most commonly used in aircrafts. A bathometer, is an instrument used for measuring water depth.
Answer: D
Q16. An existing sewer line is to be extended to a new proposed maintenance hole (MH2). The sewer line will be laid flat along the excavated ground. The proposed invert of MH2 is to be 114.22. If this proposed invert were to be lowered by 1.4 feet, the excavated slope from MH1 to MH2 would be 3%. What would be the excavated slope if the invert was lowered by only 0.8 feet?
Vvc

  • A) 1.71%
  • B) 2.52%
  • C) 2.66%
  • D) 1.74%

"Pipe layed flat" implies the slope of the pipe is the same as the excavation slope. We need to use 2 equation 2 unknowns. Equation (1) and Equation (2): \(\dfrac{\text{Rise}}{\text{Run}} = \text{Slope}\) \((1)\ldots\ \dfrac{y + 1.4}{x} = 0.03\) \((2)\ldots\ \dfrac{y}{x} = 0.022\ \therefore\ y = 0.022x\) \((1)\ldots\ \dfrac{0.022x + 1.4}{x} = 0.03\) \(0.022x + 1.4 = 0.03x\) \(1.4 = 0.008x\) \(175\ \text{ft} = x\) \((2)\ldots\ \dfrac{y}{175} = 0.022\) \(y = 3.85\) Slope if invert lowered 0.8 feet: \(3.85 + 0.8\ \text{feet} = 4.65\) \(\dfrac{\text{Rise}}{\text{Run}} = \text{Slope}\) \(\dfrac{4.65}{175} = 0.02657 = 2.66\%\)

Answer: C

Q17. A road is to be built on the edge of a township. What is the radius of the curve needed to complete the road?
VhcProgram S — partial

  • A) 752.40'
  • B) 484.25'
  • C) 481.43'
  • D) 534.16'

The most visual way to solve this is to redraw the lines where they would approximately be on the coordinate system. Find I using the tangent bearings given: \(6°12'9" + 84°15'13" = 90°27'22"\) \(180 - I = 90°27'22"\) \(I = 89°32'38"\) Find the chord length using the coordinates given: \(\text{Chord length} = \sqrt{(x_2 - x_1)^{2} + (y_2 - y_1)^{2}}\) \(\text{Chord length} = \sqrt{(10803.87 - 10333.57)^{2} + (1999.88 - 2587.18)^{2}}\) \(\text{Chord length} = 752.40\ \text{feet}\) Solve R by using the chord equation: \(C = 2R\sin\dfrac{I}{2}\) \(752.40 = 2R\sin\dfrac{89°32'38"}{2}\) \(R = 534.16'\)

Answer: D

Q19. As part of a roadway reconstruction project, a dirt parkway area is to be created into a 4' wide sidewalk. The original ground stationing and elevations are shown below. Starting at station 1+27, the FG has an elevation of 756.94 with a proposed slope of -1.75%. Determine the catch point station.
Vvc
StationOG Elev (ft)
1+27758.34
2+03757.58
3+00753.41
3+86751.23

  • A) 2+17.89
  • B) 2+92.14
  • C) 2+49.80
  • D) 2+80.39

Calculate the FG at each station: \(756.94 - (203 - 127)(0.0175) = 755.61\) \(756.94 - (300 - 127)(0.0175) = 753.91\) \(756.94 - (386 - 127)(0.0175) = 752.41\) By observation, the catch point seems to be between 2+03 and 3+00. Make sure that the slope for the OG elevation is constant throughout all stations. In this case, that is not true. Therefore find the slope for the stretch between 2+03 to 3+00 which is where we expect the lines to cross. \(\text{Slope OG } 2{+}03\ \text{to}\ 3{+}00 = \dfrac{753.41 - 757.58}{300 - 203} = -0.043\ \dfrac{\text{ft}}{\text{ft}}\) Create two equations for the slope of the OG and FG. Choose 3+00 for the x of the each equation though 2+03 can be used too. Original (Existing) grade slope equation: \(y = mx + b\) \(OG: 753.41 = -0.043(300) + b\) \(b = 766.31\) \(OG: y = -0.043x + 766.31\) Finish grade slope equation: \(y = mx + b\) \(FG: 753.91 = -0.0175(300) + b\) \(b = 759.16\) \(FG: y = -0.0175x + 759.16\) Set both equation equal to each other: \(-0.0175(x) + 759.16 = -0.043(x) + 766.31\) \(x = 280.39\) \(\text{Catch point station} = 2{+}80.39\)

Answer: D

Q21. In a mass diagram, the mass ordinate is the:
Varea
  • A) the x and y coordinate at a particular point on the mass diagram
  • B) the sum of the volumes of cut and fill up to that point on the mass curve
  • C) the point of conversion from total cut to total fill
  • D) the cumulative volume of excavation and embankment for the entire project
The mass ordinate are the individual points that makeup the mass curve representing the cumulative volume of excavation and embankment up to that station. Therefore there are an infinite number of mass ordinates that follow the mass curve.
Answer: B

Q23. On a plan and profile sheet, the vertical scale of a proposed pipeline is 1/60. The ground horizontal distance between MH1 and MH2 is 79.4'. The vertical exaggeration is 6:1. What is this horizontal distance on the plan and profile sheet?
IVphoto
  • A) 7.94"
  • B) 2.65"
  • C) 13.23"
  • D) 15.88"
Find vertical scale: \(\dfrac{1}{60} \rightarrow \dfrac{1"}{60"} \times \dfrac{12"}{1'} = 1" : 5'\) Find horizontal scale: \(\text{vertical exaggeration}: \dfrac{6}{1} = \dfrac{\frac{1"}{5'}}{\frac{1"}{x'}} = \dfrac{x}{5}\) \(x = 30 \rightarrow \text{horizontal scale} = 1" : 30'\) Plan horizontal distance: \(\text{distance} = \dfrac{79.4}{30} = 2.65"\)

Answer: B
Q24. Which of the following is another way to characterize attribute data as the term is used in GIS?
IVgis
  • A) feature class data
  • B) spatial data
  • C) key
  • D) aspatial data
An attribute is a characteristic of a spatial feature that is usually described by numbers or letters. Attributes are often stored in tabular format and are linked by keys to the feature in a relational database. A key in the GIS is a unique identifier assigned to each record in a table that helps link it to others. Attributes are aspatial, or non-spatial, data. Feature classes are collections of the same type of entities that share the same spatial and attribute data.
Answer: D

Ipls

  • B) boundary elevations on the corners
  • C) coordinates of boundaries
  • D) bearings and lengths of the boundaries
"metes and bounds" refers to measurements and land boundaries bearings and lengths. See glossary of manual.
Answer: D
Q26. A storm drain pipe is to be constructed from point A (50 feet left of sta 3+50) to point B (50 feet right of sta 5+00). The centerline radius is 600 feet. What is the length of the storm drain pipe?
VhcProgram T — partial

  • A) 179.50 feet
  • B) 163.55 feet
  • C) 600 feet
  • D) 151.70 feet

Construct a triangle using A, B, and the radius point (C) to the 600 ft radius curve. Since points A and B are radial to the centerline, angle ACB is the central angle of the horizontal curve from sta 3+50 to sta 5+00. \(L = \dfrac{2\pi RI}{360°}\) \(I = \dfrac{L(360°)}{R(2\pi)} = \dfrac{(150\text{ft})(360°)}{(600\text{ft})(2\pi)} = 14.324°\) Use Law of Cosine to solve for length AB: \(c^{2} = a^{2} + b^{2} - 2ab\cos C\) \(c = \sqrt{a^{2} + b^{2} - 2ab\cos C}\) \(c = \sqrt{(550\text{ft})^{2} + (650\text{ft})^{2} - (2)(550)(650)\cos 14.324}\) \(c = \sqrt{32{,}227.44\text{ft}^{2}}\) \(c = 179.52\text{ft}\)
Note: The direction of right or left is determined by direction of increasing stationing. Anything left of an increasing stationing is considered left of centerline and anything right of an increasing stationing is considered right of centerline.

Answer: A

Q28. A new aerial photography project is to target the area shown in the illustration. The project will use the following parameters. Assuming a North - South orientation to the flight lines, what is the minimum number of flight lines required?
IVphoto

  • A) 2
  • B) 1
  • C) 3
  • D) 4
Find ground length: \(\text{Ground length} = (\text{Format Size}) \times \dfrac{1}{\text{Photo Scale}}\) \(\text{Ground length} = 9\text{ in} \times \dfrac{12{,}000}{1} \times \dfrac{1\text{ ft}}{12\text{ in}}\) \(\text{Ground length} = 9{,}000\text{ ft}\) Find Max Distance between flight lines: \(FL_{\text{MaxDist}} = (\text{Ground Length}) \times (1 - \text{Side Lap})\) \(= (9{,}000\text{ ft}) \times (1 - 0.30)\) \(= 6{,}300\text{ft}\) Minimum number of flight lines: \(FL_{\text{Min\#}} = \dfrac{\text{Target Area Width}}{FL_{\text{MaxDist}}}\) \(= \dfrac{4.6\text{ miles} \times 5{,}280\text{ ft}/\text{mile}}{6{,}300\text{ ft}}\) \(= 3.86\) \(\text{Rounding up} = 4\)

Answer: D
Q29. If sanitary sewer line 2 (SS 2) must have a minimum clearance of 2 feet below SS 1 and +1.1% slope from manhole 4 to 5 (MH 4 to MH 5), what is the highest possible invert elevation at MH 4? (Figure in Plan View)
Vconstr

  • A) 79.91'
  • B) 80.20'
  • C) 79.34'
  • D) 80.16'

Elevation of SS1 at Sta 8+96 \(\text{Slope of pipe} = \dfrac{83.75 - 86.98}{1012 - 789} = -0.0145\) \(\text{Length from MH1 to MH2} = 896 - 789 = 107\text{ ft}\) \(\text{elevation change} = 107(-0.0145) = -1.55\) \(\text{Elev}_{SS1}\text{ at MH2} = 86.98 - 1.55 = 85.43 = \text{top of SS1 pipe}\) Invert elevation of SS2 at Sta 8+21 (Note: Station 8+96 on SS1 is at the same location as Sta 8+21 on SS2): \(\text{Invert}_{Sta\ 8+21} = 85.43 - \dfrac{9}{12} - 2 - \dfrac{0.5}{12} - \dfrac{6}{12} = 82.14'\) Invert elevation at Sta 6+41 (MH4) (Note: The arrow of a slope usually points downhill unless there is a sign in front of the number. If that is the case, the arrow points in whatever direction the sign is in. In this case, the +1.1% points towards MH5 so it is an upwards slope towards MH5. If there is no sign in front of the slope, the arrow points downhill.): \(\text{Distance}_{MH2-MH4} = 821 - 641 = 180\text{ ft}\) \(\text{Invert}_{Sta\ 6+41} = 82.14 - 180(0.011) = 80.16\text{ ft}\)

Answer: D
Q30. Line AB is measured to be 78.34' ± 0.007'. Line CD is measured to be 89.11' ± 0.012'. What is the sum of these two lines?
IIItheory
  • A) 167.45' ± 0.000'
  • B) 167.45' ± 0.019'
  • C) 167.45' ± 0.005'
  • D) 167.45' ± 0.014'
\(\text{Error of sum} = \pm\sqrt{E_{AB}^{2} + E_{CD}^{2}}\) \(\text{Error of sum} = \pm\sqrt{(0.007)^{2} + (0.012)^{2}} = 0.01389 = 0.014\) \(\text{Line AB} + \text{Line CD} = 78.34 + 89.11 = 167.45' \pm 0.014'\)

Answer: D
Q31. An aerial photograph was taken at a height of 11,500 ft above the terrain with a 6 inch focal length camera, and using a standard 9 inch x 9 inch format. What is most nearly the acreage in this photograph?
IVphoto
  • A) 5,467 acres
  • B) 3,434 acres
  • C) 1,144 acres
  • D) 6,831 acres
The acreage in this photograph is determined as follows: \(\text{Photo Scale} = \dfrac{f}{H}\) \(PS = \dfrac{6\text{in}}{11{,}500\text{ft}} = \dfrac{1\text{in}}{1{,}916.67\text{ft}}\) Ground length of one side of photo: \(L_{\text{Ground}} = (\text{Format Size}) \times \dfrac{1}{\text{Photo Scale}}\) \(= 9\text{in} \times \dfrac{1{,}916.67\text{ft}}{1\text{in}}\) \(= 17{,}250\text{ft}\) Area of photo: \(A = \dfrac{17{,}250 \times 17{,}250}{43{,}560\text{ft}^{2}/\text{acres}}\) \(= 6{,}831.1\text{ acres}\)

Answer: D
Q32. The radius of the center line of a highway curve is 2200 ft and the deflection angle to point B on the curve is 4°17'. The length of the highway from A to B is most nearly
VhcProgram S — partial

  • A) 328.94
  • B) 330.14
  • C) 164.47
  • D) 273.27
\(\dfrac{I}{2} = 4°17'\) \(I = 8°34'\) \(L = \dfrac{2\pi(R)(I)}{360}\) \(L = 328.94\text{ ft}\)

Answer: A
Q33. In order to improve the lives of the community, the City has approved a man-made recreational lake inside a 30 acre park. What type of survey is needed before construction?
Iintro
  • A) As-built survey
  • B) Topographic survey
  • C) GPS survey
  • D) Hydrological survey
As-built surveys are required after construction is completed. Hydrological survey is for existing bodies of water. This lake is proposed so there is no water or lake yet. Topographic survey will determine the current elevations and therefore would be the correct answer. GPS can be used for the topographic survey but GPS survey alone does not address the question since GPS survey is not really a type of survey but an instrument used to create a survey.
Answer: B
Q34. The survey crew is sighting two identical Philadelphia rods from an instrument, Rod-A and Rod-B, as shown in the illustrations. What are the center hair readings on each rod? Which rod is located at a higher elevation? Which rod is closer to the instrument?
IIstadia

  • A) Rod-A center hair reading: 7.42
    Rod-B center hair reading: 7.26
    Rod-A is located at a higher elevation than Rod-B
    Rod-A is located closer to the instrument
  • B) Rod-A center hair reading: 3.74
    Rod-B center hair reading: 7.54
    Rod-B is located at a higher elevation than Rod-A
    Rod-B is located closer to the instrument
  • C) Rod-A center hair reading: 7.42
    Rod-B center hair reading: 7.26
    Rod-B is located at a higher elevation than is Rod-A
    Rod-A is located closer to the instrument
  • D) Rod-A center hair reading: 7.26
    Rod-B center hair reading: 7.42
    Rod-B is located at a higher elevation to the instrument than Rod-A
    Rod-A is located closer to the instrument
The top and bottom of each tick mark count as a graduation. For Rod-A, the center hair reading is 7.42 as shown. The Rod-B center hair reading is 7.26.

The rod with the smallest center hair reading will be at the highest elevation, therefore Rod-B is located at a higher elevation than Rod-A as this value is subtracted from the height of the instrument (HI).

The stadia interval (upper hair minus lower hair) for Rod-A is less than the stadia interval for Rod-B, therefore Rod-A is closer to the instrument than Rod-B. This can also be deduced by the greater magnification see in the image for Rod-A.
Answer: C
Q35. The magnetic declination of line PQ is 6°17'56"E with a magnetic bearing of N23°22'14"W. If 50 years ago, the magnetic declination was 1°13'12"W, the magnetic bearing 50 years ago was
IIIang
  • A) N15°51'6"W
  • B) N26°2'46"W
  • C) N18°17'30"W
  • D) N17°4'18"W

True bearing never changes. Remember that the line does not move on a coordinate plane. The declination changes which changes the magnetic bearing reading but the line never moves. The magnetic bearing is measured from the magnetic declination line as if the declination was the true north line. \(23°22'14" - 6°17'56" = 17°4'18"\) \(N17°4'18"W = \text{true bearing}\) \(17°4'18" - 1°13'12" = 15°51'6"\) \(N15°51'6"W = \text{magnetic bearing 50 years ago}\)

Answer: A

Q37. For the points shown,
(x, y) for Point E = (1000 ft, 1000 ft)
(x, y) for Point D = (900 ft, 1600 ft)
bearing CE = N78°14'29"E
distance CE = 167.49 ft

  • B) S5°45'38"W
  • C) S84°14'22"W
  • D) N5°45'38"E

\(90° - 78°14'29" = 11°45'31"\) \(\sin 11°45'31" = \dfrac{y}{167.49}\) \(y = 34.13\text{ft}\) \(\cos 11°45'31" = \dfrac{x}{167.49}\) \(x = 163.98\text{ft}\) \(C(x,y) = (836.03, 965.87)\) \(\tan\theta = \dfrac{900 - 836.03}{1600 - 965.87}\) \(\theta = 5°45'38" = N5°45'38"E\)

Q38. On a map, two contour lines are 1.5 cm apart and the contour interval is 1 meter. If the map scale is 1:2000, what is the slope between these two contours?
IVtopo
  • A) 1.50%
  • B) 0.15%
  • C) 5.00%
  • D) 3.33%
Find the ground distance then divide the elevation change by the distance: \(\dfrac{1}{2000} = \dfrac{1.5\text{ cm}}{d}\) \(d = 3000\text{cm} = 30\text{ meters}\) \(\text{Grade} = \dfrac{\text{rise}}{\text{run}} = \dfrac{1}{30} = 0.033 \rightarrow 3.33\%\)

Answer: D
Q39. The elevation of the toe of the slope at sta 19+50 is
VvcProgram P — partial

Of course CL stands for centerline and TYP means typical, as in that exact one is typical of others in that area. \(19{+}50 - 5{+}00 = 1450\text{ft}\) \(elev_{19{-}50} = \dfrac{Rx^{2}}{2} + g_1 x + elev_{BVC}\) \(R = \dfrac{g_2 - g_1}{L} = \dfrac{3.5 - 5.5}{24} = -0.08333\) \(elev_{19{-}50} = \dfrac{-0.08333(14.5)^{2}}{2} + 5.5(14.5) + 250\) \(elev_{19{-}50} = 320.99\text{ft}\) \(toe = 320.99 - (22 \times 0.02) + 0.5 + (10 \times 0.02)\) \(toe = 321.25\text{ft}\)

Answer: D

Q40. The radius of the arc is 750 ft. The area of the shaded region is
Vhc

  • B) 12.90 acres
  • C) 6.45 acres
  • D) 3.37 acres

\(AB = BC = 750\text{ft}\) \(\angle ACB = S88°15'18"W - S41°48'32"W\) \(\angle ACB = \angle CAB = 46°26'46"\ (\text{isosceles triangle})\) \(\angle ABC = 180° - 46°26'46" - 46°26'46"\) \(\angle ABC = 87°6'28"\) \(\dfrac{\sin 87°6'28"}{b} = \dfrac{\sin 46°26'46"}{750}\ (\text{Law of Sine})\) \(\text{or}\) \(C = 2R\sin\dfrac{I}{2} = 2(750)\sin\dfrac{87°6'28"}{2}\) \(\text{chord} = b = 1033.55\text{ft}\) \(HSO = R\left(1 - \cos\dfrac{I}{2}\right)\) \(HSO = 750\left(1 - \cos\dfrac{87°6'28"}{2}\right)\) \(HSO = 206.46\text{ft}\) \(750 - 206.46 = 543.54\) \(\text{area of triangle} = \left(\dfrac{1033.55}{2}\right)(543.54)\) \(\text{area of triangle} = 280888\text{ft}\) Area of Shaded Region = Area of Pizza Slice − Area of Triangle: \(\pi(750)^{2}\left(\dfrac{87°6'28"}{360}\right) - 280888 = 146701\text{ft}^{2}\) \(\dfrac{146701\text{ft}^{2}}{43560\text{ft}^{2}/\text{acres}} = 3.37\text{ acres}\)

Q41. If 90 percent of all contours on a map must be within 2.5 feet error, what contour interval is necessary?
IVtopo
  • A) 1.25 ft
  • B) 2.5 ft
  • C) 10 ft
  • D) 5 ft
According to the National Map Accuracy, no more than 10% of the elevations can be in error of more than 1/2 contour. Therefore if 90% of the elevations must be within 2.5 ft, 2.5 ft would be equal to 1/2 contour which means the full contour interval is 5 ft.
Answer: D
Q42. A vertical curve L=1800 ft, G1=−1.4%, G2=+3.7%, EVC at sta 75+27, elev 157.61 ft. What is the elevation at sta 71+33?
VvcProgram P — full

  • A) 145.23 ft
  • B) 129.87 ft
  • C) 165.93 ft
  • D) 173.24 ft
Find elevation of the PVI, working back from EVC: \(elev_{EVC} = elev_{PVI} + g_2\left(\dfrac{L}{2}\right)\) \(157.62 = elev_{PVI} + 3.7\left(\dfrac{18}{2}\right)\) \(elev_{PVI} = 124.31\text{ ft}\) Find elevation of BVC: \(elev_{BVC} = elev_{PVI} - g_1\left(\dfrac{L}{2}\right)\) \(elev_{BVC} = 124.31 + 1.4\left(\dfrac{18}{2}\right)\) \(elev_{BVC} = 136.91\text{ ft}\) Station of BVC: \(sta\ BVC = 75{+}27 - 1800 = 57{+}27\) Elevation on the curve at sta 71+33 (x = distance from BVC, in stations): \(elev_x = \dfrac{R \cdot x^{2}}{2} + g_1 \cdot x + elev_{BVC}\) \(x = 7133 - 5727 = 1406\text{ ft} = 14{+}06\) \(elev_x = \left(\dfrac{3.7 + 1.4}{18}\right)\dfrac{(14.06)^{2}}{2} - 1.4(14.06) + 136.91\) \(elev_x = 145.23\text{ ft}\)

Answer: A
Q43. A proposed sewer line is to be constructed on the curve below. The radius of the curve that connects the two manholes is 100 feet. Vconstr

  • C) sta 33+01

\(X = \sqrt{100^{2} - 77^{2}} = 63.80\text{ft}\) \(\text{Station at EC } MH1 = 33.65 - 0.6380 = 33.0120 = 33{+}01.2\)
Note: Rt of centerline and Lt of centerline mean right and left of the centerline. The direction of right or left is determined by direction of increasing stationing. Anything left of an increasing stationing is considered left of centerline and anything right of an increasing stationing is considered right of centerline.

Q46. This active remote sensing technique in Lidar is similar to radar but uses
IIlidar
  • A) laser light pulses
  • B) direct photos
  • C) radio waves
  • D) GPS
LiDAR shoots out 50,000 to 100,000 light pulses and measures the time it takes for the laser to bounce back to establish the distance to the ground.
Answer: A
Q47. In the figure, the dashed line represents the existing ground, the solid lines represent a new road section. If the cross sections between sta 15+00 and 16+00 stay constant, the quantity of earth work is
IIIarea

  • A) 735 yd³ cut
  • B) 1470 yd³ cut
  • C) 593 yd³ fill
  • D) 1143 yd³ fill
The top number represents the elevation at that point. The bottom number represents the distance from the centerline. Use the Coordinate Method. Pick a point and proceed clockwise. \(0(56 - 56) = 0\) \(-15(54 - 57) = 45\) \(-17(63.5 - 56) = -127.5\) \(-20(61.5 - 54) = -150\) \(0(59.5 - 63.5) = 0\) \(20(54 - 61.5) = -150\) \(17(56 - 59.5) = -59.5\) \(15(57 - 54) = 45\) \(\sum = -397\) \(\text{cross sectional area} = \dfrac{-397}{2}\) \(\text{cross sectional area} = |-198.5| = 198.5\text{ft}^{2}\) Multiply by length of road section: \(\dfrac{198.5(100)}{27} = 735\text{ yd}^{3}\text{ cut}\)

Answer: A
Q48. A department store is scheduled to be built on a plot of land. In order for there to be enough clearance, the current road must be detoured with an offset of 40 ft. The radius must remain 2000 ft for each equal curve. How much longer is the road between points A and B than before the offset?
VhcProgram S — partial

  • B) 0.95 ft
  • C) 10.70 ft

\(\text{Tangent offset} = R(1 - \cos I)\) \(20 = 2000(1 - \cos I)\) \(I = 8°6'35"\) \(x\text{ distance for one arc} = r\sin I\) \(x\text{ distance for one arc} = 282.14\text{ ft}\) \(D = 282.14 \times 4 = 1128.56\) \(\text{arc distance for one arc} = 2\pi R \times \dfrac{8°6'35"}{360°}\) \(\text{arc distance for one arc} = 2\pi(2000) \times \dfrac{8°6'35"}{360°}\) \(\text{arc distance for one arc} = 283.08\text{ ft}\) \(\text{total arc distance} = 283.08 \times 4 = 1132.32\text{ ft}\) \(\text{Difference} = 1132.32 - 1128.56 = 3.76\text{ ft}\)

Answer: D

Q51. You are a project engineer early in the pre-design process of a major two-block development project. A site layout has been prepared and a parking lot will be completed as the first stage of the proposed improvements. You currently need to identify possible overhead utilities. What should you do?
Iintro
  • A) Conduct a field investigation
  • B) Call USA
  • C) Contact the contractor
  • D) Mark plans for potholing
To identify possible overhead and underground utilities, a field investigation is needed to locate where they may exist. USA or Dig Alert is called before construction to locate the lines a few days prior to construction. Potholing is used to measure the depth of underground utilities. The contractor for the project likely has not been hired yet at this stage of the project.
Answer: A
Q52. Which of the following will not affect the use of an EDM
IIfield
  • A) Buildings in the area
  • B) Light wave interference
  • C) Asphalt interference
  • D) Radiowave interference
Physical barriers such as a building will influence the accuracy of an EDM. Also there are many different types of EDMs but some of them rely on high-frequency radio waves while other use the velocity of light to determine distance. Thus any interference with either of these two will affect EDM accuracy. Asphalt does not directly affect EDM accuracy.
Answer: C
Q53. What is the correct order for the use of the surveys and staking for an engineering project?
Iintro
  • A) Boundary, Control, As-built, Construction Staking
  • B) Control, Boundary, Construction Staking, As-built
  • C) Construction Staking, Boundary, Control, As-built
  • D) As-built, Construction Staking, Control, Boundary
A project starts with a control survey that will be the basepoints for the topographic survey. In this case topographic survey was not an option but a boundary survey could be conducted to identify the limits of work. Afterwards, construction staking is used to mark specific locations (involving grading, cut/fill, etc.) of the project where engineering work will be completed. Finally when all work is completed, an as-built survey is completed to record final elevations of the new engineering work.
Answer: B

Assume that the grade is constant from sta 0+00 to sta 2+00: \(\text{slope} = \dfrac{\text{difference in elevation}}{\text{distance}}\) \(= \dfrac{91.15\text{ft} - 88.00\text{ft}}{\text{sta } 0{+}75 - \text{sta } 0{+}00}\) \(= \dfrac{3.15\text{ft}}{75\text{ft}}\) \(= 0.042\) The HI at sta 1+75 is 94.70 ft: \(\text{elevation at sta } 1{+}75 = HI - FS\) \(= 94.70\text{ft} - 2.10\text{ft}\) \(= 92.60\text{ft}\) \(\text{grade at sta } 1{+}75 = 91.15\text{ft} + (\text{sta } 1{+}75 - \text{sta } 0{+}75) \times (0.042)\) \(= 91.15\text{ft} + 4.2\) \(= 95.35\text{ft}\) \(\text{fill} = \text{grade} - \text{elevation}\) \(= 95.35\text{ft} - 92.60\text{ft}\) \(= 2.75\text{ft}\)

Q55. The centerline of a road has a length of 1000 feet as shown. If a storm floods this road and reaches an elevation of 360 feet, what length of the vertical curve would be under water?
VvcProgram P — partial

  • A) 900 feet
  • B) 860 feet
  • C) 1000 feet
  • D) 930 feet

Start by calculating the BVC and EVC elevations: \(elev_{BVC} = elev_{PVI} - G\left(\dfrac{L}{2}\right)\) \(elev_{BVC} = 342.76 + 2.5\left(\dfrac{10}{2}\right) = 355.26'\) \(elev_{EVC} = elev_{PVI} + G'\left(\dfrac{L}{2}\right)\) \(elev_{EVC} = 342.76 + 4.6\left(\dfrac{10}{2}\right) = 365.76'\) The flood elevation is above the BVC. The flood elevation is below the EVC. Thus, we can conclude that the entire left side of the vertical curve is underwater and that a portion of the end of the curve is above the water elevation. (So you already know that 1000 ft cannot be the answer. Cross it off) To find the total length underwater, find the distance from the BVC to the point on the curve that is at elevation 360. \(elev_x = \dfrac{Rx^{2}}{2} + Gx + elev_{BVC}\) \(R = \dfrac{G' - G}{L} = \dfrac{4.6 + 2.5}{10} = 0.71\) \(360 = \dfrac{(0.71)x^{2}}{2} - 2.5(x) + 355.26\) \(x = -1.5534\ \text{or}\ x = 8.5956\) \(x = 8.60\ \text{stations} = 860\text{ ft}\)
Note: A problem like this is one of the main reasons that a TI-89 is useful. When finding x, the solve function in the TI-89 can do this quickly - press F2 --> option 1 for solve(. For this solution you would enter solve(360=0.71*x^2/2-2.5*x+355.26,x). You should see x=-1.55336 or x=8.59562 as the answers. If you do not use a TI-89, you need to use the quadratic formula to find the x values. Of course a distance cannot be a negative answer so that answer choice is invalid.

Answer: B
